summary: Finance in Business Central covers general ledger and accounting, dimensions, currencies, receivables, payables, bank reconciliation, VAT, withholding and excise tax, cost accounting, inventory costs, cash flow, period closing, E-Documents, consolidation and financial analytics. It answers setup and how-to questions for day-to-day bookkeeping, period-end work and reporting.
overview:
Finance in Business Central starts with core accounting: the chart of accounts, posting groups, payment terms and methods, dimensions and currencies. On top of that sit the daily cycles for receivables, payables and bank reconciliation, followed by period-end work such as closing periods and years.

Tax topics are split between a dedicated VAT subtopic and the Finance area's own pages. The own pages cover vendor and employee withholding tax, viewing withholding tax entries, and excise tax registration. Further subtopics cover cost accounting, inventory costing, cash flow forecasts, prepayment invoices, E-Documents, and multi-company consolidation and intercompany. Financial analytics is the biggest subtopic, with 129 pages.

For orientation, start with the Financial management overview and the Accounting and bookkeeping guide. Then go to the subtopic that matches the task. Accountants who work across companies should read the Accountant experiences page for the Accountant Role Center and the Company Hub.
key_points: The Accountant Role Center gives access to financial pages and reports. External accountants can be invited, and the Company Hub supports work across multiple companies.
Accounting setup covers the chart of accounts, payment methods, payment terms, posting groups and payment tolerance.
Vendor withholding tax is calculated on purchase invoices and orders from vendor, item and G/L account setup, once minimum thresholds are met.
Employee withholding tax uses posting setup with a Gross or Net calculation base, thresholds accumulated by period, and expense category settings.
The Withholding Tax Entries page shows base amount, tax amount, posting groups and party type for vendor and employee transactions.
Excise tax registration for goods such as fuel, alcohol and tobacco tracks tax amounts without creating G/L entries.
Subtopics cover period closing, G/L, dimensions, currencies, receivables, payables, bank reconciliation (including Copilot-assisted matching), VAT and E-Documents.
Cost accounting, inventory cost management, cash flow forecasting, prepayments, financial analytics, and consolidation with intercompany transactions each have their own subtopic.

issues: The overview opens with "Finance is the largest functional area in Business Central". No source supports this. The sources only show that Financial analytics is the largest subtopic within Finance (129 pages).
The overview uses the phrase "this hub's own pages", which breaks the no "This hub" style rule. Reworded to refer to the Finance area's own pages.

Small point: the last key point calls the subtopic "multi-site consolidation". That is a loose label for the Multi-site and international organizations subtopic, which covers consolidation and intercompany transactions. Reworded to match.

All other claims are supported by the source summaries. That includes the withholding tax details, excise tax without G/L entries, Copilot-assisted bank matching, external accountant invitations and the Company Hub.
